COAL SWITCH 2022

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We uncover a coal switch scam that in part contributes to South Africans being plunged into darkness with loadshedding.

Unique Selling Point:
- A LOADSHEDDING STORY THAT's NOT A LOADSHEDDING STORY - TADAAAA :)
- A CRIME TREND
- AN INVESTIGATION
- CONFRONTS

Summary:
Opportunistic criminals target transport company drivers to switch loads of export grade coal with a lower grade. The driver pockets cold hard cash. And the receivers, sell the loads of coal again into the export market for a second time.

We expose the intricate scam and confront some of the buyers of the stolen coal.

Further information:
HOW THE SCAM WORKS
1. Transporters will be contracted to move tons of coal from a mine (POINT A) to a processing plant or power station or railway station for export (POINT B).
2. Collection slips are issued when the trucks are loaded at POINT A with the weight loaded.
3. At POINT B –delivery notes are issued when the loads are dropped off, again with the weight.
4. BUT what they pick up from POINT A doesn’t make it to POINT B.
5. Drivers are approached by a middleman to drop the load off at another location along the route between A & B for a fee of up to R10000 cash.
6. They swop out the good grade coal for a lower grade coal and the driver sets off to Point B.


HOW BIG IS THE PROBLEM?
This is not an isolated problem – coal theft plagues the industry across South Africa. The black market for coal is thriving because there is a huge demand for coal locally and for export. So if you can get a cheap load that you can sell at premium prices – dodgy dealers are willing to look the other way. It is affecting mines every where – there are task teams, and investigators all over trying to get to the bottom of this crime trend.

HOW DO WE KNOW IT’S HAPPENING?
TECHNOLOGY!
Some transporters have installed sophisticated tracking systems that not only monitor the trucks movements, but also when exactly the cargo is off loaded. When the tipping mechanism on the truck is engaged a video camera is activated recording the physically delivery along with the GPS co-ordinates of the drop off.

The weight is also recorded – when the switch out coal, it’s not accurately reloaded so often by the time it gets to Point B there is a discrepancy in the amount of coal that gets delivered.

HOW DID THIS BECOME KNOWN?
Some of the mines have had their international clients reject the coal received. Lab tests show that the grade of coal delivered is not what was paid for.

A RETROSPECTIVE INVESTIGATOR
Transport PI Danie Day was approached by client that was delivering the coal for a mine to the harbor for export. They have identified four key locations were coal was in fact switched – they can prove it with the GPS locations, the tipping data, video clips and discrepancies in weight of the loads that is recorded with special technology.

THE ROGUES
Our 2019 story exposed a single buyer at the time – a Jaco Venter. Guess what, he’s back at it.

We already know he what his defense is going to be – he claims it was staff that he fired in June. But never fear – I’ve got us covered – with proof of additional loads that were switched at this yard in August!

HOW DO WE TELL THE STORY?
- We explain the crime trend and impacts.
- We follow the trial of the investigation, the discoveries
- We include the technology showing how solid the evidence is against the drivers
- Footage of the tipping of the stolen coal
- Creative Maps showing the movement of the trucks and deviations.
- We then confront the buyer

INDUSTRY EXPERT – POERIE VAN ROOYEN
Poerie van Rooyen heads up the coal theft investigations for a group of mines and has been working in this particular field for the last decade. He will explain the black market and how the coal gets traded – that it is a national issue, that often power stations end up paying twice for the same load and in some cases end up receiving substandard loads that impact on the running of power stations and contribute to breakdowns.

CONFRONT – CHASING THE LEADS
We visit all four sites and go looking for Jaco Venter for old time sake.

INTERVIEWS
- TRANSPORTER
- DRIVER - HIDDEN ID - EXPLAIN HOW THEY GET APPROACHED AND HOW MUCH THEY GET PAID
- PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR - DANIE DAY - HOW THEY CAUGHT THE DRIVERS AND ID-ed THE LOCATIONS
- MINING INDUSTRY INVESTIGATOR - BIGGER PICTURE, CRIME TRENDS
- COAL EXPERT – XAVIER PREVOST – WHY DOES THE GRADE MATTER TO SOUTH AFRICANS
- CONFRONTS

STRUCTURE: COAL SWITCH

VO: COAL. Despite a dirty reputation. It’s in demand - here in SA, and globally - a demand, that’s fuelling an illicit trade.

DANIE: It is HUGE. It's a very big economic sabotage.

LINK: The black market for coal is booming. Thousands and thousands of tons of the commodity sold load by load by load, hitting the economy and pushing the load shedding crisis.

VO: But syndicates aren’t stealing loads out right – no, the latest crime trend is much more devious.

Coal gets transported along South African roads every day from mines, destined for power stations, siding yards for export, or furnaces used by local industry. But what gets loaded at Point A doesn’t always make it to Point B.

VO: This is coal theft 2.0. The kingpins make big money and will do anything to avoid exposure…

UPSOUND MAC CHASING CAR.

VO: But, to take this story forward, we first need to take a step back.

The kingpins send out scouts targeting drivers – this man was recruited at a
truck stop.

DRIVER: The guy who approaches me. he says there is a deal like this. You switch , the coal, you tip a little bit. Then we add you another one. Then you go.

VO: It’s called coal switching. The drivers offload a high grade of coal at a yard pointed out by the scout, they then load a low grade of coal instead - usually under the cover of darkness.

DRIVER: He said once I finish the deal, then I give you something. I1m6
MAC: How much did he offer?
DRIVER: Ah just R13,000. the payment they put in my account,it just come there and there.

LINK: No overhead costs, no maintenance costs, no fuel costs. Using his employer's truck, he sells a load of coal he doesn't own to a third party. He just pockets the money.

VO: But the driver isn't the one pocketing the big money. It’s an organised network of receivers - they coin about R100 000 per load.
--

VO: Middlemen sell the high grade coal for about R1500 per tonne to dodgy coal yards.

This premium coal can fetch up to R6000 a tonne on the export market, while the swopped low grade discard coal goes for under a R100 a tonne. The margins on stolen coal are truly criminal.

LINK: Dodgy buyers are snatching up the switched coal and they sell it straight back to the legitimate market at full price, making massive profits.

VO 12: But it goes beyond the broader financial impacts of coal theft - it affects YOU in your home. Xavier Prevost is a Coal Quality Expert.

MAC: // Is it in any way contributing to load shedding?
XAVIER: Yes, I think it's the main reason. // Because we're damaging the power stations .M12 // if you put diesel in your petrol car, you will ruin that. Okay. Same thing applies with the boiler. The boiler if it wants Grade A, If you put grade B, you cause major damage to the boiler. M3

VO 12: The result is extensive maintenance and repairs that costs Eskom billions of rands frustrating South Africans with ongoing power outages.

VO: But beyond our borders, coal switching also impacts global perception.

XAVIER: We are increasing our exports tremendously. // M10 this issue of qualities and grades that coal can get swapped, can be stolen // is actually very damaging to // the industry, because then we will be seen overseas // as people that are not reliable because we are selling this and we are giving that. M10

VO 12: At least 8 big shipments failed quality tests on delivery overseas. The losses run into billions of Rands this year alone.

The mines are holding the transporters liable. And that can have catastrophic consequences for people like Jabu Ngwenya .

JABU: // We've lost contracts. // I1M11// It demoralizes you as a person.I1M10.// I’m the one who’s falling because I’m small.

VO 9: Even though his drivers stole, the company is contractually responsible. They transported coal for export earlier this year as sub-contractors - but when the shipment was rejected, the mine came knocking.

JABU: // I was shocked that the. That THE CLIENT had to hit me with a 8 million penalty.
MAC: 8 million?
JABU: EIGHT million. I spent sleepless night. I don't know what can happen.. // I1M11
MAC: Its business will be able to survive.
JABU: NO! I can't. //. I'm busy with legal and trying to get advice. What could I do? How to minimize this damage. //. I1M13

VO: Realising his company drivers are on the take, he called in transport industry PI Danie Day.

DANIE: The cases that we have investigated is solid// We've got informants, // We have collaborated // TRACKING movement reports as well as a unit that we've got in the trailers that can tell us exactly where. What longitude, latitude.

VO: After weeks of interrogating the evidence, Day is confident that the case is water tight.

The technology not only tracks the locations, it actually records when the coal is switched out, the quantity and exactly how much is reloaded, at an exact location .

In these graphs – you can clearly see the weight dip – that’s when the coal was dropped. Sometimes the thieves don’t even reload the full amount – not only cheating on quality but also short-changing the quantity that eventually gets delivered to the actual client.

MAC: So without a shadow of doubt, your case is tight in terms of where the switching is happening.
DANIE: Multiple loads were delivered in the same area where a load has been delivered, offloaded and switched. We can prove that beyond reasonable doubt. I2M2

VO: This is Mpumalanga, it’s coal country…it's not unusual for trucks to go in and out of yards. But as it turns out, it’s also not unusual for drivers to sell their loads.

DRIVER: there by the truck stops, I hear the story, people are talking it's a common thing. // even some of the guys, the feel proud. This thing is dirty money.

VO: Analysing the data, Day has identified two (HTH & Parsons ) key sites along the R35 road in the Middleburg region where coal was switched out.

MAC: did you think these guys are doing this thing? Is it an opportunistic crime or this is actually a syndicate operating?
DANIE: I think the first few times that they've done it was just obvious to see everything works and see if they could get away with this and to identify some loopholes. But obviously soon thereafter it became syndicate orientated,

VO: This yard was linked to a company - HTH COAL . Operated by Clerrence Holtmann .

MAC: Hey tell me bra, who's the owner here?
WORKER: He’s not available
MAC: // But who’s the owner you don't know.
WORKER: Clerrence // He’s the owner of the yard. I1M2

VO: Apparently we just missed him… so we called instead.

MAC: There's some serious allegations that have been levelled against you on coal switching. So we just wanted to give you a right of reply because we’re here at your yard
CLeREeNCE: No, no, no, it’s not against me.
MAC: Who is it against?
CLERENCE: No, but I don’t switch, I buy the coal, the guy that’s supplying me with coal, I'll phone him so that he come to me
MAC: Yeah, but this is your yard. You must also come answer
CLERENCE: Yes, I will .
MAC: Okay. Must we wait for you here?
CLErENCE: I will just find out by him where’s he..
MAC: No, no, don't worry about him. This is your yard.
CLERENCE: I’m paying him for the coal, I’m not paying truck drivers for coal. I’m not stealing coal.
MAC:: Okay, then. Come. Let's. Let's talk. Let's talk.
CALL CUTS.
MAC: He’s dropped the phone.

VO: We wait, but Clerrence and his supplier are no shows.

MAC: We’re Still waiting for you - It's 30 minutes now.
CLERRENCE: //I'm just calling my lawyer because I buy my coal from a mine and then I process it and then now you come in my yard and you make like you want.
MAC: We never went into your yard Clerrence.
CLERENCE: Hey, my people told me what you did man…
MAC: We're standing outside.
CLERENCE: Speaking to everybody like you want.
MAC: We're standing outside.
CLERENCE: Now, You're making my name bad by my clients.
MAC: Clerrence. Clerrence, listen, listen, listen, Clerrence.
CLERRENCE: I am not even the one stealing coal. Who are you to make my name bad.
MAC: We're not making your name. Bad trucks came here. They switched coal. We've got the evidence, We've got the data, we've got the GPS locations. So don't tell us that we're making your name bad…
CLERENCE: Shouting – you are making my name bad.
MAC: We can when we come out. We come in with evidence. When we come out, we come with evidence. You all come in like I live in Jo'burg. Why would I come to Middleburg in the middle of nowhere for nothing. //
CLERENCE: I’ll let me lawyer phone you..

VO: But his lawyers never did. And the evidence doesn’t lie - a number of loads were switched out in this area.

The second location leads us to Jaco Venter - you might remember him from our 2019 coal theft investigation - despite being linked to stolen loads, he claimed to source coal legitimately.

UPSOUND OLD STORY _ CB 2019
MAC: how much are you buying it for?
JACO: 10 cent
MAC: 10 cents for what?
JACO: per truck//
MAC: You getting a truck load for 10 cents
JACO: my prices and off take agreements are confidential – so you know what, to be honest with you – it has nothing to do you with you, not with you, not with you, not with any Tom, Dick or Harry – it has nothing to do with no one.

VO: Except - when it’s stolen coal. Almost four years later, it seems he’s still doing dodgy deals - this new investigation shows multiple loads were switched in Venter’s yard, all hours of the day .

When he spotted the cameras - he ducked inside the office.

MAC: Ah, Jaco. Venter! Hello Jaco!
KNOCKING
Hello Jaco! So he's run away and close the door now. So he’s closed the blinds.//
MAC: Jaco! Come Jaco, don’t hide from me. You remember me from last time?

VO: We hear a car starting at the back of the building - someone is making a run for it…

CAR DRIVING OFF
MAC: Oh, it's not him. // Jaco! Jaco! Kom Jong!
CAR SPEEDS OFF

VO: But it seems it was a decoy – Jaco continues to hide in the office - Ignoring our phone calls and messages.

But the facts can’t be ignored.

MAC: How sure are we that the trucks came here and dropped off.
DANIE: Definitely 100% sure. All GPS co-ordinates and all the other separate tracking satellite devices confirmed same//
MAC: Old Friend, why do you think is running away from us?
DANIE: And he's just got something to hide most probably hey? M5

VO: We eventually received messages from Jaco and Clerrence declining a right of reply. You’ll note the wording is identical.

JABU: A CRIME that have been created that it's me who is liable. // I'm depressed most of the time because things are not moving as quick as I can to bring these people to the books.

VO: These coal swopping incidents are not isolated – it’s a crime trend that affects mines everywhere – and it’s not going to stop unless the whole value chain is investigated.


END

ADDITIONAL INFO
JACO VENTER implicates a man by the name of Kobus in a voice note he sent to a current associate explaining what happened with the last Carte Blanche and the new investigation - he blames an employee for the coal switching - he says Kobus worked night shift - Jaco claims all the switching incidents happened at night (MAY 2022) at his yard and says he chased Kobus away when he realised what he was up to. He says that he chased him away in June 2022.

We contacted Kobus Wolmerhans (ID9402225110088) // 0815526820 - have a recording - Kobus denies the allegations, says he wants nothing to do with Venter, and claims that Venter owes him money. I sent a follow up message asking for ROR - he replied on whatsapp denying allegations and distancing himself from Jaco Venter - he claims in a whatsapp that he left Venter’s employment end April 2022. Have Screen shot

In addition, I further made enquiries with other investigators and confirmed two more incidents in August 2022 - one out right theft and one switch - confirmed the location as Parson with GPS co-oridinates. I have the supporting statements. Schalk Burger from Universal Mines - 0823360637

ROY: // it's so lucrative at the moment. // it is widely spread.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We uncover a coal switch scam that in part contributes to South Africans being plunged into darkness with loadshedding.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: - A LOADSHEDDING STORY THAT's NOT A LOADSHEDDING STORY - TADAAAA :) - A CRIME TREND - AN INVESTIGATION - CONFRONTS
metadata.Summary: Opportunistic criminals target transport company drivers to switch loads of export grade coal with a lower grade. The driver pockets cold hard cash. And the receivers, sell the loads of coal again into the export market for a second time. We expose the intricate scam and confront some of the buyers of the stolen coal.
metadata.Further information: HOW THE SCAM WORKS 1. Transporters will be contracted to move tons of coal from a mine (POINT A) to a processing plant or power station or railway station for export (POINT B). 2. Collection slips are issued when the trucks are loaded at POINT A with the weight loaded. 3. At POINT B –delivery notes are issued when the loads are dropped off, again with the weight. 4. BUT what they pick up from POINT A doesn’t make it to POINT B. 5. Drivers are approached by a middleman to drop the load off at another location along the route between A & B for a fee of up to R10000 cash. 6. They swop out the good grade coal for a lower grade coal and the driver sets off to Point B. HOW BIG IS THE PROBLEM? This is not an isolated problem – coal theft plagues the industry across South Africa. The black market for coal is thriving because there is a huge demand for coal locally and for export. So if you can get a cheap load that you can sell at premium prices – dodgy dealers are willing to look the other way. It is affecting mines every where – there are task teams, and investigators all over trying to get to the bottom of this crime trend. HOW DO WE KNOW IT’S HAPPENING? TECHNOLOGY! Some transporters have installed sophisticated tracking systems that not only monitor the trucks movements, but also when exactly the cargo is off loaded. When the tipping mechanism on the truck is engaged a video camera is activated recording the physically delivery along with the GPS co-ordinates of the drop off. The weight is also recorded – when the switch out coal, it’s not accurately reloaded so often by the time it gets to Point B there is a discrepancy in the amount of coal that gets delivered. HOW DID THIS BECOME KNOWN? Some of the mines have had their international clients reject the coal received. Lab tests show that the grade of coal delivered is not what was paid for. A RETROSPECTIVE INVESTIGATOR Transport PI Danie Day was approached by client that was delivering the coal for a mine to the harbor for export. They have identified four key locations were coal was in fact switched – they can prove it with the GPS locations, the tipping data, video clips and discrepancies in weight of the loads that is recorded with special technology. THE ROGUES Our 2019 story exposed a single buyer at the time – a Jaco Venter. Guess what, he’s back at it. We already know he what his defense is going to be – he claims it was staff that he fired in June. But never fear – I’ve got us covered – with proof of additional loads that were switched at this yard in August! HOW DO WE TELL THE STORY? - We explain the crime trend and impacts. - We follow the trial of the investigation, the discoveries - We include the technology showing how solid the evidence is against the drivers - Footage of the tipping of the stolen coal - Creative Maps showing the movement of the trucks and deviations. - We then confront the buyer INDUSTRY EXPERT – POERIE VAN ROOYEN Poerie van Rooyen heads up the coal theft investigations for a group of mines and has been working in this particular field for the last decade. He will explain the black market and how the coal gets traded – that it is a national issue, that often power stations end up paying twice for the same load and in some cases end up receiving substandard loads that impact on the running of power stations and contribute to breakdowns. CONFRONT – CHASING THE LEADS We visit all four sites and go looking for Jaco Venter for old time sake. INTERVIEWS - TRANSPORTER - DRIVER - HIDDEN ID - EXPLAIN HOW THEY GET APPROACHED AND HOW MUCH THEY GET PAID - PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR - DANIE DAY - HOW THEY CAUGHT THE DRIVERS AND ID-ed THE LOCATIONS - MINING INDUSTRY INVESTIGATOR - BIGGER PICTURE, CRIME TRENDS - COAL EXPERT – XAVIER PREVOST – WHY DOES THE GRADE MATTER TO SOUTH AFRICANS - CONFRONTS
